name: Mbe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Pohlig, James 1981. Description of the Mbe verb system (ms, 115pp, Cross River Mbe [mfo]); Bamgbose, Ayo 1966/67 Mbe phonology notes, Afrika und Uebersee 50. Neither online.

sources.citation: Bamgbose, Ayo. 1967. Notes on the phonology of Mbe. Journal of West African Languages 4(1): 5-11.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing. Seven-page phonology sketch (syllable structure CV/V/CVC, consonants, vowels, syllabic nasal, tone). Sec. 5 Tone System, p. 11: five tonemes High, Low, Rising, Falling, Downstep; the words stress/accent never occur.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288
sources.note: Comparative survey; tone table gives Mbe 'H, L' citing Pohlig (2006) 'Statement of Mbe phonology, with remarks concerning orthography. Electronic ms.'; no stress discussion for any language.

sources.citation: Wei, Wei & Rachel Walker. 2020. A lookahead effect in Mbe reduplication: Implications for Harmonic Serialism. Linguistic Inquiry 51(4): 845-859. doi:10.1162/ling_a_00364
sources.note: Nothing on stress; remarks only that open-syllable monophthongs lengthen under high tone in certain verb forms (p. 854, citing Bamgbose 1967c).

sources.citation: Walker, Rachel. 2000. Nasal reduplication in Mbe affixation. Phonology 17(1): 65-115. doi:10.1017/S0952675700003833
sources.note: OT analysis of Mbe reduplication built on Bamgbose's data; sec. 3.3 treats tone (noun-stem tones distinctive, Class 2 verb tones not, p. 81 fn. 11). 'Stress' appears only in discussion of other languages (Nivens 1993 data, Tuyuca); no statement about Mbe stress.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE inventory 1285 (Mbe, mbee1249; source Bamgbose 1967) and inventory 1599 (source Pohlig 1981)
sources.note: Segment inventories with tone marks (1285: H, L, HL, LH; 1599: H, L); PHOIBLE records no stress information.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. Comparative Ekoid (Ekoid-Mbe wordlists and notes). Ms., formerly at rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/Bantoid/Ekoid/Comparative
sources.note: Blench's Ekoid-Mbe comparative notes cite Pohlig's materials and may summarise Mbe prosody; the rogerblench.info domain is now hijacked and web.archive.org is could not be reached by automated download (an Internet Archive copy dated 2026-09-14 exists).
